Hobby: Advanced Hiking and Multi-Day Trekking

Based on the profile of Alex, an avid hiker seeking to upgrade from basic gear to high-quality equipment for challenging, multi-day treks, here is a detailed budget plan. This plan focuses on durability, weight reduction, and performance, which are critical for advanced hiking.

### 1. Initial Investment (One-Time Costs)

This category covers the essential gear upgrades required to safely and comfortably undertake multi-day treks. Prices are estimated based on mid-to-high-end market rates for reputable brands (e.g., Osprey, Gregory, MSR, Big Agnes, Merrell, Salomon).

| Item | Description | Estimated Cost Range (USD) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **High-Quality Hiking Boots** | Waterproof, ankle-supporting, durable leather or hybrid materials for rugged terrain. | $150 - $250 |
| **Durable Backpack** | 50-70 liter capacity, internal frame, hip belt with pockets, rain cover included. | $200 - $350 |
| **Lightweight Tent** | 2-3 person capacity, freestanding, <3 lbs weight, weather-resistant (e.g., 3-season). | $300 - $600 |
| **Sleeping Bag** | Down or synthetic insulation, rated for 20°F (-6°C) or lower for variable conditions. | $150 - $400 |
| **Sleeping Pad** | Insulated inflatable or foam pad for comfort and ground insulation. | $80 - $200 |
| **Cooking System** | Lightweight stove, fuel canister, and compact pot set. | $50 - $100 |
| **Water Filtration** | Pump filter or gravity filter system for safe drinking water on multi-day trips. | $40 - $100 |
| **Navigation & Safety** | Topographic maps, compass, headlamp with extra batteries, first-aid kit, emergency whistle. | $50 - $100 |
| **Clothing Layers** | Moisture-wicking base layers, insulating mid-layers (fleece/down), waterproof shell jacket/pants. | $200 - $400 |
